documents.body:
Spring check, his usual timing.

Asthma — rescue inhaler twice since the fall. No night waking.
Rhinitis — on daily fluticasone, doing fine heading into grass season.
SM — no flushing or reactions. Cromolyn PA went through in January.
Anxiety — steady, not discussed at length.

Meds/allergies reviewed, no changes.

Exam: comfortable, nares clear, lungs clear with normal air entry, heart regular.

A/P: allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis controlled; systemic mastocytosis stable. Continue everything. Physical in August.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM — 36M

Interval history: no reactions this year, no ED or urgent visits. Saw the allergist in the spring; nothing changed. Albuterol rarely. Nose controlled. Ready for the school year.

Current meds: cetirizine 10 daily, famotidine 20 BID, cromolyn oral 200 mg QID, fluticasone nasal daily, albuterol PRN, epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector x2.
Allergies: bee/wasp venom (anaphylaxis), latex (anaphylaxis), dust mite, Timothy grass.

GAD-7 6. PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 1. Nonsmoker.

Exam: Pleasant, in no distress. Head and neck normal, no nodes, thyroid not palpable. Heart sounds normal, regular rhythm. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin: no urticaria. No edema.

Plan:
1. CBC, CMP, lipids today (last lipids 2021).
2. Fall flu and COVID shots.
3. Tdap next year.
4. Continue all meds.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — regional hospital
Date of visit: 07/22/2026, arrived 15:50 via ambulance. Observation unit overnight; discharged 07/23/2026 09:30.

Chief complaint: collapsed after multiple insect stings.

History: 37-year-old man with systemic mastocytosis and a prior ED visit in 2023 for hypotension and bronchospasm during a dental procedure. Today he was working in his backyard garden on a warm afternoon. Per the neighbor who called 911, he was stung several times, grabbed at his chest and went down moments later.

PMH: systemic mastocytosis; allergic asthma; persistent allergic rhinitis; generalized anxiety disorder.
PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood; wisdom teeth removed.
Medications: epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector PRN, cetirizine 10 mg daily, famotidine 20 mg BID, albuterol HFA PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID.
Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis; latex — anaphylaxis; dust mite; Timothy grass.
Family history: father with severe Hymenoptera allergy and hypertension; mother asthma and allergic rhinitis; sister atopic dermatitis and food allergies; paternal uncle systemic mastocytosis.
Social: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month, high school math teacher.

Arrival vitals: BP 75/45, HR 120, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air.

Exam on arrival: Obtunded. Skin flushed. Periorbital swelling. Diffuse wheezing in both lung fields. Extremities cool, capillary refill delayed. No sign of trauma; no seizure activity witnessed or observed. Multiple sting sites; no retained stingers.

ED course: Nonrebreather oxygen, supine positioning, two large-bore IVs. Initial crystalloid bolus without blood pressure response. Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM anterolateral thigh at 15:58, repeated at 16:03. Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and methylprednisolone 125 mg IV given. Nebulized albuterol for the wheeze. By 16:12 BP 104/66, HR 108, becoming responsive and following commands; mentation back to baseline over the next hour, wheeze resolved.

Results: ECG sinus tachycardia, no ST changes. High-sensitivity troponin I normal at arrival and on 2-hour repeat. CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Observation: held overnight on monitor for possible biphasic reaction. No recurrence.

Discharge vitals 07/23 09:15: BP 122/76, HR 84, SpO2 98% on room air.

Diagnosis: Anaphylaxis following multiple insect stings, in a patient with systemic mastocytosis.

Discharge: home on his usual medications. See PCP within one week. Return at once for recurrent symptoms; use epinephrine first.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to hear it from me — got stung a bunch in the garden yesterday and passed out. Spent the night in the ED, they gave me two shots of epi plus IV meds. Home now and feel OK, just exhausted. They said to see you within a week.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm glad you're home and that you messaged. Front desk will put you in Tuesday morning. Please rest, keep both pens on you even indoors, and if anything starts again use the pen and call 911 first, me second. I'll ask the ED to send their record.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit.

7/22 — multiple stings while gardening, collapsed. In the ED: obtunded, BP 75/45, HR 120, flushed, periorbital swelling, diffuse wheeze, cool with delayed cap refill. Fluids alone didn't move the pressure; IM epinephrine x2 plus IV diphenhydramine, famotidine, methylprednisolone and nebulized albuterol. ECG sinus tach without ST changes, troponins normal, CBC/BMP normal. Overnight observation, no biphasic reaction, home 7/23. ED record reviewed in full.

Today: feels back to himself. No hives, no wheeze, no chest symptoms. Taking cetirizine, famotidine and cromolyn as prescribed. Understandably shaken: GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 4. Not asking for medication.

Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis; latex — anaphylaxis; dust mite; Timothy grass.

Exam: BP and HR normal today. No facial swelling. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur.

A/P:
1. Anaphylaxis after insect stings, 7/22 — resolved. New epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector two-pack sent today; carry both everywhere, outdoors included.
2. Systemic mastocytosis — second severe systemic reaction in three years. Referral placed to allergy/immunology for an expedited visit; I'll send them the ED record and my note.
3. Allergic asthma — quiet now.
4. GAD — up after this; we'll keep checking in.
Physical already booked for September.

documents.title: School form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Our school nurse wants a signed form saying I carry an epinephrine auto-injector and what to do if I react at school. Can you fill out the attached? Also — haven't heard from the allergy clinic yet about an appointment.

documents.title: RE: School form
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Form signed and attached: epinephrine 0.3 mg IM to the thigh at the first sign of a serious reaction, call 911, keep your second pen nearby. Front desk checked with the allergy clinic — they have the referral and are working on a date. If you don't hear by early September let us know and we'll push.
